findings.finding: Lower (floor-row) steps are evenly spaced light bars crossed by full-height vertical rail posts, so the bottom third reads a little like a rack or ladder cage rather than solid stone steps; tread/riser rhythm does not compress toward the top enough below the arch.
findings.fix: Below the arch, give each riser 2px of the darker stone with a 1px shadow line under the nosing. Make the lower treads 3px and the upper ones 2px. Shorten the inner rail posts so they stop at the newel cap instead of crossing every tread.

findings.finding: The red runner is a flat single-tone strip; it does not break at each nosing, so it reads as a painted stripe and not as a carpet over steps.
findings.fix: On each riser, darken the runner one step and add a 1px light highlight at each tread nosing. Put the brass rod pixel exactly at the riser/tread junction.

findings.finding: The north rail is drawn in elevation as a balustrade (top bar plus vertical balusters at full height), with tall corner newels. At 1x the piece reads as an upright stone fireplace or alcove frame standing on the floor, not as a hole in the floor seen from above. The rails look as tall as a door lintel, not low.
findings.fix: Draw the north rail as a 2px cap band seen from above (light top, 1px dark under-edge). Show balusters as 1px stubs at most, reduce the corner newels to 2x2 cap squares, and run the west/east rims as 2px top-view caps along the full depth. Add a 1px floor-shadow line on the room floor just north of the rail.

findings.finding: The tread darkening is clear, but the side inner walls are barely visible, so the hole does not visibly narrow with depth.
findings.fix: Add a 1-2px darker wedge on the west and east inner walls, widening northward.

findings.finding: The lower oak steps are large flat mid-orange faces with thin dark lines, so they read like stacked crates or drawer fronts. The light nosings are lost in the lower half.
findings.fix: Add a 1px light nosing at the top of every lower step and make each riser one shade darker than the tread above it, so the tread/riser alternation continues down to the floor row.

findings.finding: Between two oak bookshelves of the same timber colour, the oak frame and steps at 1x can read as one more shelf unit; only the lit top step separates it.
findings.fix: Push the doorway interior one shade darker behind the steps, add warm light spill on the top two treads, and make the frame posts a 1px darker timber than the bookshelves.

findings.finding: The speckled grey treads and the straw/dropping pixels are busier than the texture density of the existing chipset; at 1x the steps go noisy.
findings.fix: Cut the grain speckle to 2-3 pixels per tread and keep the straw to one cluster on one tread.

findings.finding: Same problem as castle-down. The wooden north rail with balusters and tall corner posts is drawn in elevation, so the piece reads as a standing wooden frame, gate or fireplace. In the shipped owlery at 3x it looks like a wooden doorframe on the floor next to the west wall, not a stairwell you descend.
findings.fix: Turn the rails into top-view caps: a 2px oak cap band on north/west/east with a 1px dark under-edge, corner posts as 2x2 cap squares, no full-height balusters. Keep the hole interior and the darkening treads as they are.

places.finding: Owlery: the new down stairwell at (1,8) is the only way out of the room, and because of its upright-frame look a player standing south of it does not see an exit going down (same issue as wz-owl-stair-down, counted once there).
places.fix: Fixed by the owl-stair-down top-view rail redraw. Optionally add a slightly darker floor shadow ring around the hole.

places.finding: Clock tower: the stair now sits flush against the west end of the north wall, and the frame's west edge touches the wall pilaster with no gap. That is acceptable, but the iron frame's bottom posts end abruptly on the dark floor with no base or shadow.
places.fix: Add a 1px darker floor shadow under the bottom newels and a 1px iron foot plate.
